_about: Site-specific interpretive text for notebook 03's summary.json (Liwa). Every string is a Python format template filled from this run's numbers (vs, nd, ph, s30, l30, ws, qc, P, n_dunes, pct_below, tt: see the seih_al_hama file). Written after looking at this site's notebook 02 and 03 results; ranges quoted literally (heights) are from the 2026-11-15 run. Rewritten 2026-11-15 for the registration-reference bracket (02_registration_reference.md).

published.reference: Lorenz, Radebaugh, Barnes & Turtle, EGU2016-9369; Lorenz & Radebaugh 2015 (Planetary Dunes Workshop 8003); Pugh, Glennie & Williams 1993 (AAPG abstract)
published.their_value: ~0.1 m/yr for the 50-80 m Liwa megadunes (a field inference from overrun date palms, abstracts only); the smaller northern dunes 'migrate southward more rapidly than the draa' (no number)
published.our_value: megadune bodies: not measured (the body-scale matcher failed its known-shift test, notebook 02 section 15b), and with the registration reference itself uncertain by about +-{qc[registration_reference][reference_systematic_per_component_myr]:.2f} m/yr their motion is below what this method can resolve here; small dunes and bedforms: {vs[detected_speed_median_myr]:.2f} m/yr median toward {ph[field_median_heading_deg]:.0f} deg (2013-2025), {qc[registration_reference][dune_field_by_reference][bare_in_farms][detected_speed_median_myr]:.2f}-{qc[registration_reference][dune_field_by_reference][hard_outside_farms][detected_speed_median_myr]:.2f} m/yr depending on the registration reference
published.note: Consistent with the published direction (south-south-east) and with small dunes moving much faster than the megadunes are reported to move, but not a test of the 0.1 m/yr: that rate is below what this method can resolve here, and the megadune bodies are not measured.

wind_agreement_note: mean |heading - RDD| over detected windows, RDD {ws[RDD_deg]} deg (MERRA-2 2000-2024). The regime is close to unimodal (RDP/DP {ws[RDP_DP]}): the field-median heading {ph[field_median_heading_deg]} deg is {ph[field_heading_minus_modes_deg][0]} deg from the strongest sand-moving mode (toward {ph[wind_mode_toward_deg][0]} deg) and {ph[field_heading_minus_RDD_deg]} deg from RDD; per-window median difference {ph[per_window_abs_heading_minus_RDD_median_deg]} deg. Year-to-year field speeds follow the MERRA-2 drift (r {qc[interannual][wind_correlation][pearson_r]}).
second_dataset_note: HLS S30 (Sentinel-2, independent geolocation) and L30 (same Landsat instruments) are registered on the same two canopy-free references as Landsat, on their own 30 m grids (S30: {s30[registration]}; L30: {l30[registration]}). S30: field headings {s30[heading_difference_deg]} deg apart, r {s30[corr_E]} E / {s30[corr_N]} N, {s30[field_median_speed_hls_myr]} vs {s30[field_median_speed_landsat_myr]} m/yr. L30: headings {l30[heading_difference_deg]} deg apart, {l30[field_median_speed_hls_myr]} vs {l30[field_median_speed_landsat_myr]} m/yr. In all three sensors the farm canopy drifts against canopy-free ground by ~0.2-0.45 m/yr toward the north-north-west.
limits: Detected dune windows move a median {vs[detected_speed_median_myr]:.2f} m/yr (10-90 %: {vs[detected_speed_p10_p90_myr][0]:.2f}-{vs[detected_speed_p10_p90_myr][1]:.2f}, max {vs[detected_speed_range_myr][1]:.2f}) toward {ph[field_median_heading_deg]:.0f} deg; {pct_below:.0f} % of valid dune windows move below the detection limit (median {nd[detection_limit_median_myr]:.2f} m/yr).

These speeds are relative to a registration reference that is itself uncertain. The farm canopy, the only stable ground used before, drifts toward the north-north-west (toward the anti-sun direction) and is not used. The speeds are measured against the mean of two canopy-free references (paved roads and buildings outside the farms; bare ground inside the farms), which differ by {qc[registration_reference][dune_field_by_reference][hard_outside_farms][detected_speed_median_myr]:.2f} vs {qc[registration_reference][dune_field_by_reference][bare_in_farms][detected_speed_median_myr]:.2f} m/yr in the median dune speed. Half their difference ({qc[registration_reference][reference_systematic_per_component_myr]:.2f} m/yr per component) is included in the uncertainty and the detection limit. On the farms alone the median would have been {qc[registration_reference][dune_field_by_reference][stable_ground (not used)][detected_speed_median_myr]:.2f} m/yr.

Megadune bodies (up to ~110 m of relief) are not measured: the body-scale matcher failed its known-shift test, so no body speed is reported. The motion in the velocity grid, the dune polygons and the reach years is that of the small dunes and the bedforms riding over the megadunes, not of the megadunes themselves.

Reach years forecast the migration of dune forms (slip-face advance), not wind-blown sand crossing a road, which happens wherever a road borders loose sand, whatever the dunes do (see borders_free_sand in targets.geojson).

At the median speed (~{vs[detected_speed_median_myr]:.1f} m/yr) one 15 m pixel is about a decade of motion, so reach years for targets near the sand carry an edge uncertainty of +-7.5 m plus the outline uncertainty of the target.
Most targets are not reached by {P[projection_end]}; targets flagged 'sand at edge now' already have migrating sand within that edge uncertainty.
The projection is advection along the measured 2013-2025 motion, assuming those conditions continue; it does not model dune deformation, merging, splitting or growth.
Vegetation, windbreaks, sand fences, levelling, construction and climate change alter the outcome; many farm edges here are walled.

Motion is measured in 480 m windows: it is the motion of the small dunes (spacing ~{qc[linearity_aliasing][dune_spacing_25pct_variance_below_m]}-{qc[linearity_aliasing][dune_spacing_spectral_peak_m]} m) and sand sheets inside, not of a single dune body.
Only {n_dunes} dunes (13-31 m high) are outlined from NASADEM (February 2000) at bedform scale; they are medium dunes, mostly in the northern field, not megadunes.

The second dataset confirms the direction but not the speed: HLS S30 and L30 (30 m red band, registered on the same canopy-free references) give {s30[field_median_speed_hls_myr]:.2f} and {l30[field_median_speed_hls_myr]:.2f} m/yr against {s30[field_median_speed_landsat_myr]:.2f}-{l30[field_median_speed_landsat_myr]:.2f} m/yr for Landsat pan over the same years. At the other two sites L30 agrees with pan within ~0.1 m/yr. Until this is understood, the pan speed magnitude here has no independent confirmation.
The published ~0.1 m/yr for the megadunes is a field inference far below what this method can resolve here: no numeric comparison is possible.
MERRA-2 wind is a ~0.5 x 0.625 deg reanalysis of hourly means; absolute drift potential is approximate.
Farm targets are vegetated plots (HLS NDVI, last year) plus OSM farmland; built-up targets are OSM buildings and residential areas; unmapped or abandoned plots are not targets.
Results are valid for this box (the eastern Liwa crescent, not Liwa town) and 2013-2025 only; nothing outside the box is assessed.
